chapter: Lee Collins and the riverboat Washington
title: Sun White's band on the boat and newspaper headlines
summary: He gives size of the boat band and tells of making headlines and ruffians.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Who were these guys you were playing with on the board?
That was Sun White but he had Gordett. See Gordett was Tillman's brother-in-law, you understand?
How many pieces did you use on that band?

We had five. And then we had another guy by the name of Dixon, sometime we'd have him working but he played bass. He could play up some bass but he took with a stroke in his hand. And so that'd be him. And he couldn't make it.

No, not on the board. That's why I made headlines with all them papers. Started to, you know, start putting my name in the papers. Brother of my dreams, I love you. I mean all them numbers was out. Brother of my dreams and all them waltzes and all that stuff like Wayne King used to play at that time. And you made headlines? I mean all the papers all up and down them rivers, you understand? The boat, like you say, couldn't hardly hold the people, you understand what I mean? And there used to be some ruffians on that boat, they used to carry on it so bad, they cut out that excursion from the Howard and Boyd to Johnville. Some people was bass. You know when their bass don't go on that tight you know they're bass. But I had a chance to go through that way with another band one time and them guys met me and Faraday and they found me some liquor from somewhere, they remembered me, if I did something they remembered too. And we had a nice time.
